prompt:
These ideas were found in different parts of one discussion about: PEP 698: A typing.override decorator
Some are the same idea written differently.

0. Specifying the parent class in the decorator [rejected] - if in a single commit you move a method from one base to another, you as the author are likely aware of what you did, so the safety benefits are relatively small; I'm guessing there wouldn't be too much use of this feature. Since it's relatively easy to implement this capability using runtime logic in a library, that makes me thing we don't need to bake it into typing.py all of the type checkers.
1. Requiring the decorator for abstract method overrides [rejected] - I'm not sure there is much need for special treatment of abstract methods. The PEP recommends type checkers support a strict mode where all method overrides must be marked with the decorator, whether abstract or not.
2. Adding runtime enforcement logic to the decorator [rejected] - I'm guessing there wouldn't be too much use of this feature. Since it's relatively easy to implement this capability using runtime logic in a library, that makes me thing we don't need to bake it into typing.py all of the type checkers.
3. Providing a shim for third-party override decorators [accepted] - One way of handling this kind of thing is to do a typing.TYPE_CHECKING shim, like so: from typing import TYPE_CHECKING if TYPE_CHECKING: from typing import override as override else: def override(func):
4. Main proposal for @typing.override decorator [accepted] - The SC has decided to accept this PEP!

Group the numbers that describe the SAME idea. Every number must appear in exactly one group; an idea
with no duplicate is a group of one. Give each group the clearest, most specific title.

groups.title: Rejecting built-in runtime enforcement or parent-class specification due to low utility and library-level implementability
Requiring the decorator specifically for abstract method overrides (rejected in favor of a strict mode option)
Accepted proposals: providing a TYPE_CHECKING shim for third-party decorators and adopting the main @typing.override decorator
